A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiODE-GAN research. All nine pages of v1 and nineteen pages of v2 were readable, including equations, figures, tables, and v2 Appendices A–B. v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original G12EC classification results, generative-model comparisons, and experiments varying classifier architecture, synthetic sample count, and loss weighting.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds PTB-XL results, physiological and distributional analyses, and an LVSD clinical evaluation in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The WaveGAN/WGAN-GP backbone and both Euler-loss components remain. The stated formulation introduces a separate Euler-penalty weight, lambda_EUL, in v2 Equation 14, whereas v1 Equation 20 uses unit weight. v2 also expands the conditioning description from diagnostic class to class plus RR duration; corresponding implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: G12EC coverage is retained. v2 adds PTB-XL evaluation and a separate paired ECG–echocardiogram patient cohort for LVSD detection, defined by ejection fraction below 50% (Section 6.2 and Appendix B).

E2.justification: v2 adds ME-GAN to the main generative-model comparison while retaining DCGAN, WaveGAN, SimGAN, and SSSD-ECG. Appendix B additionally introduces physician and senior-physician benchmarks, substantially extending the comparison scope beyond generative methods.

E3.justification: The reported 80/20 split changes from ECG records in v1 to patients in v2; this establishes a protocol-description revision, not that experiments were rerun. v2 adds AUROC/AUPRC evaluation, inter-lead MSE and feature-space KL/MMD procedures, and a clinical protocol with a balanced 854-patient test set and six physician readers.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct analyses of physiological consistency through inter-lead MSE, distributional alignment through KL/MMD, and real-versus-synthetic waveform overlays (Sections 6.3–6.4). The existing classifier, loss-weight, and synthetic-sample-count analyses remain; moving the last to Appendix A is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 adds ± quantities to specificity results, although their interpretation as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals is unspecified. Five-fold paired t-testing and the p < 0.05 criterion already appeared in v1; v2 clarifies comparisons against the real-only classifier without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds PTB-XL, AUROC/AUPRC, physiological-consistency, distributional, waveform, and clinical results. New Table 6 reports real-only/augmented specificity of 0.78/0.81 at sensitivity 0.78. Among retained entries, SimGAN IRBBB specificity changes from 0.88 to 0.87; MultiODE-GAN NSIVCB is consistently 0.76, resolving v1's 0.75/0.76 discrepancy across Tables 1–2. The revised split description prevents interpreting these entries as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Formal changes are limited to the separately weighted generator objective and expanded conditioning definition. The McSharry ODE system, Euler discretization, and limb-lead identities remain mathematically equivalent. v2 adds no theorem, proof, or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The central physiological GAN contribution remains, but v2 extends the introduction and conclusion from potential diagnostic usefulness to claimed retrospective clinical utility for LVSD screening and comparison with cardiologists. The abstract also replaces broad accuracy language with a specific claim about specificity improvements.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning computational cost, dependence on labeled beats for EDM fitting, difficulty generating entirely novel conditions, and limited gains near performance ceilings. It also explains Euler discretization as a local consistency operator and interprets the new physiological and clinical evaluations. v1's explicit future-work goal of extending heartbeat generation to full recordings disappears.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents training-only least-squares EDM fitting, 300-sample beats with cropping/padding, classifier optimizer and training budget, validation-based threshold selection, a 2:1 synthetic-to-real ratio, and clinical hyperparameter tuning. These materially expand reproducibility information, although some precise classifier filter, kernel, and initialization details from v1 are omitted. The open-source availability claim is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ME-GAN, PTB-XL, evaluation metrics, and heart-failure clinical context, while removing the He et al. ResNet reference. Its positioning remains an extension of SimGAN with physiological inter-lead constraints, with a sharper distinction from purely data-driven diffusion methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized, a limitations section and appendices are introduced, and the existing sample-count analysis moves to Appendix A. This exceeds routine language editing.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column journal layout, substantially redraws the architecture diagram, and merges v1 Tables 1–2 into an expanded comparison table. It adds several results tables and waveform overlays, while redrawing and relocating existing ablation plots.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single-benchmark evaluation and incomplete training documentation, v2 improves reproducibility and assessment through clearer implementation details, patient-level split reporting, PTB-XL, and threshold-independent metrics. However, new Table 4 reports unexplained unequal MSEs for algebraically equivalent limb-lead residuals, Appendix B's split counts total 13,824 rather than the stated 13,820, and Table 1's ± quantities remain undefined. These issues limit the evidential strength of the expanded physiological and clinical claims, leaving a supported but limited net quality improvement.
